# Transfer Any File (文件格式任意转换助手)

> Transfer Any File is an open-source Chrome extension (Manifest V3, MIT licence) that converts files between 14 formats — Markdown, HTML, Word (.docx), PDF, TXT, CSV, Excel (.xlsx), JSON, PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, GIF, SVG — entirely on the user's own machine. It requests one permission (`storage`), its own code issues no network request of any kind (asserted on every push by `pnpm verify:offline`), and it works with the network disabled. Batch conversion of mixed source formats, an optional merge that folds a batch of images into one multi-page PDF, automatic multi-step conversion chains over 48 direct routes, per-file error isolation with copyable failure diagnostics, split preview with inline editing, a recently-used group in the target picker, ZIP download, and a local conversion history.

Primary language: the product page is bilingual with an in-page Chinese / English switch; the privacy policy carries both languages on one page. Neither needs a server. Interface languages: English and Chinese; with no stored choice the extension follows the browser language (a `zh*` browser gets Chinese, anything else English), and an explicit choice is remembered. Names: `Transfer Any File` is the brand and the repository name, used unchanged in English surfaces; Chinese surfaces (interface, product page, README, store listing in its default language) call it 文件格式任意转换助手.
Category: productivity / file conversion. Price: free, no paid tier, no ads, no account.

## Product page

- [Product page](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/): Formats, how a conversion is routed, features, comparison with online converters, install steps, FAQ, technical details, contact
- [Privacy policy](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/privacy.html): Bilingual (EN / 简体中文) — no data collection, no transmission, on-device storage only
- [File diff](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/diff/): Interactive — drop in two files (or paste two texts) and the line and word-level diff is computed in the visitor's own browser. The only page on this site that takes a file as input; it is a byte-for-byte copy of `tools/file-diff.html`, which is the file the offline guards actually open, and no code in it issues a request

## By source format

One hub per source format: every open target, the exact route it walks, what the route keeps and what it drops, and the targets the policy greys out. A cell in the format matrix without a pair page of its own links to the matching hub anchor.

- [Markdown conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown/): all ten open targets from .md, with the HTML hop behind Word and PDF called out
- [HTML conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html/): Word, Markdown, plain text, PDF and the rest of what an .html page reaches
- [Word conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/word/): from .docx to Markdown, HTML, PDF and the other open targets, with mammoth → HTML as the shared first hop
- [PDF conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf/): text extraction, per-page images, and the PDF → data targets that stay greyed out by design
- [Excel conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/excel/): CSV, JSON, HTML, PDF and the document routes, including multiple sheets in one output
- [CSV conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv/): spreadsheets, JSON and the document/image routes, with the value-preservation rules that keep `00123` intact
- [TXT conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt/): every open target, and why TXT → Markdown only wraps the text in a fence
- [JSON conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json/): CSV, Excel and the document routes, including the synthetic `_value` column for rows with no key to hang on
- [PNG conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/png/): JPEG, WebP, PDF, HTML, Markdown and Word, plus the image → text/data targets greyed out by policy
- [JPEG conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/jpg/): PNG, WebP, PDF, HTML, Markdown and Word, with transparency flattened only where the target demands it
- [WebP conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/webp/): PNG, JPEG, PDF, HTML, Markdown and Word, including the animated-WebP first-frame limit
- [BMP conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/bmp/): PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF, HTML, Markdown and Word; BMP itself is input-only
- [GIF conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif/): first-frame routes to PNG, JPEG, PDF, HTML, Markdown and Word, with frame loss disclosed when the file really animates
- [SVG conversions](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/svg/): rasterized routes to PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF, HTML, Markdown and Word, with scripts and remote references removed first

## Route-by-route detail

Every page below states, for one source→target pair, what the route actually executes, which structures survive, which are dropped and why, and the limits that apply. Each is bilingual with the same Chinese / English switch as the product page.

- [All conversion pages](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/): index of the routes people ask about, with the full format matrix
- [Markdown → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-word.html): two steps through HTML, and the result is real Word paragraphs rather than a screenshot; data-URI images travel, relative paths stay relative, remote images are stripped before packing
- [Word → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/word-to-markdown.html): mammoth reads the semantic structure; embedded images arrive as data URIs, layout-only features stay behind
- [Markdown → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-html.html): a complete HTML document with its CSS inlined, GFM tables and task lists; scripts, event handlers and remote references are stripped before the file is written
- [HTML → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-pdf.html): rendered at 800 px in a sandboxed iframe, then sliced onto A4 as lossless PNG pages — no text layer, and remote images are never fetched
- [Word → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/word-to-pdf.html): Word → HTML → PDF, rasterized page by page onto A4 — no text layer, and the pagination is not Word's own
- [Markdown → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-pdf.html): marked → HTML → A4 page slices; identical on every machine, and nothing in the file selects or searches
- [PDF → TXT](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf-to-text.html): pdf.js extracts the text layer in reading order and link annotations are protocol-filtered; a scanned PDF has no text layer, and there is no OCR
- [PDF → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf-to-html.html): the same text layer rejoined as paragraphs and headings instead of a flat .txt; the PDF's own bookmarks become `<h1>`–`<h6>` at their outline depth, a short all-caps line becomes an `<h2>` when there is no outline, link annotations survive as `<a>` behind a scheme allowlist (`javascript:` and `data:` are removed)
- [PDF → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf-to-docx.html): two steps through HTML with no intermediate on disk — Word opens it as an altChunk and lays the text out itself, so the paragraphs are editable but the pagination is Word's, not the PDF's
- [Word → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/docx-to-html.html): mammoth reads meaning rather than appearance, so Heading 1–4 become `<h1>`–`<h4>`; body text, lists, links, tables and embedded images arrive in one self-contained file, while layout-only Word features stay behind
- [HTML → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-docx.html): sanitized HTML is packed as an altChunk that Word renders on open; inline SVG becomes a PNG first, and remote images, stylesheets and fonts are stripped before packing
- [HTML → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-md.html): Turndown plus a whole-table GFM rule — pipe tables, task checkboxes and rasterized inline SVG survive; cell formatting and CSS do not
- [HTML → Text](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-txt.html): a reading-order walk where lists keep their numbers and `start` value, links keep their URL, and text hidden by CSS is still extracted
- [TXT → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-md.html): fenced as a code block with nothing changed — the fence sizes itself one backtick longer than the longest run in the text, so an embedded snippet cannot close the block early; no guessing at headings or lists
- [Excel → CSV](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/excel-to-csv.html): cell values rather than display text, ISO-shaped dates, a UTF-8 BOM, formula injection escaped, one CSV per sheet inside a ZIP
- [CSV → Excel](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-excel.html): a field becomes a numeric cell only when it round-trips exactly, so `00123` and a 20-digit account are not silently rewritten
- [Excel → JSON](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/excel-to-json.html): one sheet becomes an array of row objects, a workbook becomes an object keyed by sheet name; dates arrive as the ISO text the reader rendered rather than as day serial numbers
- [CSV → JSON](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-json.html): every field is read as text first, so `00123` survives intact; a field regains number type only when parsing and re-printing return identical characters within 15 significant digits
- [JSON → CSV](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-csv.html): the header is the union of every object's keys; nested values go into the cell as JSON text rather than being flattened away
- [JSON → Excel](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-excel.html): a two-step route through CSV, so both directions share the same value rules; nested objects and arrays are written into the cell as JSON text
- [Excel → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/xlsx-to-pdf.html): every worksheet laid out in sequence behind its own heading, cell values as display text with dates normalised before the A4 raster — formulas arrive as their cached result, and the output carries no selectable text
- [Excel → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/xlsx-to-html.html): every sheet as its own table behind an `<h2>`, dates rendered as text and formulas as their cached result; one self-contained HTML with no scripts and no Excel styling
- [PNG → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/png-to-webp.html): alpha kept; quality and a target file size are honoured by stepping quality first, then the longest edge
- [PNG → JPEG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/png-to-jpg.html): transparency flattens onto white, and the same quality / target-size order applies with the longest edge as the second lever
- [JPEG → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/jpg-to-png.html): decoded and re-encoded locally into a lossless container — worth doing before editing a photo, not to recover detail the encoder already discarded
- [JPEG → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/jpg-to-webp.html): a second lossy pass, so it pays in bytes and costs in detail, with the same quality and target-size dials as PNG → WebP
- [WebP → JPEG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/webp-to-jpg.html): for recipients that will not accept WebP; alpha flattens onto white, and decode-then-encode is a generation of loss
- [WebP → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/webp-to-png.html): decoded and re-encoded as a lossless PNG with alpha intact; an animated WebP contributes its first frame only, and that loss is not counted separately
- [WebP → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/webp-to-pdf.html): one image per page at the image's own pixel size (96 DPI), transparency flattened onto white, and no text layer; a batch of mergeable images can be ticked into a single multi-page PDF instead of one PDF each (up to 200 pages)
- [PNG → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/png-to-pdf.html): the pixels go in losslessly, with no redraw (only a picture past 8192 px on an edge is resampled), and the page takes the image's own dimensions rather than A4; one PDF per image by default, or one merged multi-page PDF for the whole batch
- [PNG → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/png-to-html.html): the original bytes embedded as a data URI — no re-encode, so alpha, pixels and metadata stay intact in one self-contained page
- [JPEG → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/jpg-to-pdf.html): the one image → PDF route that does re-encode, once, at quality 0.92 onto white; a batch gets one PDF per image by default, and the “Merge into one PDF” box folds it into a single document (one page per image, up to 200 pages) instead
- [SVG → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/svg-to-png.html): re-rendered as vectors at the target size, with scripts, event attributes and remote references removed before rasterization
- [SVG → JPEG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/svg-to-jpg.html): the same vector render landing on white — size taken from `width` / `height`, then `viewBox`, then a 1024 px square when neither reads as a usable number
- [SVG → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/svg-to-webp.html): the same rasterisation leaving by a different door, and the difference is the container — a transparent icon stays transparent instead of being laid on white first
- [PDF → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf-to-png.html): one lossless image per page, named by its document page number, at a chosen density of 96 / 144 / 200 / 300 DPI (144 by default); there is no quality step and no target size on this route, and each page is painted white before rendering, so nothing coming out of a PDF carries transparency
- [PDF → JPEG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf-to-jpg.html): one image per page named by its document page number, at a chosen density of 96 / 144 / 200 / 300 DPI (144 by default) rasterised along the vector render path, with a direct edge rather than a lossless PNG detour
- [PDF → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf-to-webp.html): the same per-page render with a WebP encode at the end; quality steps and a target size act only at that final encode
- [GIF → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif-to-png.html): the first frame losslessly re-encoded, with the palette's transparent index becoming a real alpha channel — and frame loss disclosed only for files that genuinely animate (the GIF block structure is walked to find out)
- [GIF → JPEG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif-to-jpg.html): the first frame laid onto white and encoded as a still JPEG; frame loss is flagged for genuinely animated GIFs, and transparency cannot survive the target
- [BMP → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/bmp-to-png.html): a lossless re-encode of an almost-uncompressed container, so the picture is unchanged while the file usually drops by an order of magnitude; 8-bit palettes expand to RGBA during decode
- [BMP → JPEG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/bmp-to-jpg.html): the largest size gap on this product line, and part of it is information genuinely discarded — quality steps of 40%–90% and a target size are chased quality-first, pixels-second
- [HTML → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-png.html): the whole page rather than a viewport — rendered in a sandboxed iframe, measured, and returned as one image as tall as the content actually is; non-UTF-8 sources decode UTF-8 → GB18030 → GBK so mojibake is never photographed
- [CSV → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-pdf.html): each row and column reaches an HTML table that is then sliced into A4 pages; values and dates render as the cells hold them, and the PDF carries no text layer
- [Excel → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/excel-to-word.html): one editable Word table per worksheet, with the sheet name as a heading in multi-sheet workbooks; charts, fills and formulas stay behind in Excel
- [PDF → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/pdf-to-markdown.html): text items ordered by position on the page, link annotations restored behind a scheme allowlist, no OCR — a scanned page has no text to extract
- [SVG → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/svg-to-pdf.html): the SVG is normalised, stripped of active content and rasterised onto a page sized to its pixels, so the PDF holds a bitmap rather than vectors
- [Word → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/word-to-png.html): the document renders through HTML to one long image, with the longest edge settable; it does not follow Word pagination, so use Word → PDF then PDF → image for page-by-page output
- [WebP → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/webp-to-word.html): the original bytes go inside the .docx as a data URI, so it opens without a file alongside and fetches nothing; the picture is not read as text
- [TXT → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-pdf.html): the file lands in one `<pre>` block, so indentation and ASCII alignment keep their character positions, then the page is cut at the A4 aspect ratio — a rendered image, with no text layer
- [Word → TXT](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/docx-to-txt.html): ordered lists are renumbered from item position, tables come out tab-separated and links carry their target as `[url]`; a DOM walk, not a regex tag-strip
- [GIF → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif-to-pdf.html): the first frame is re-encoded onto white and laid on a page sized to its pixels, and only a GIF with a real second image descriptor is reported as losing frames
- [SVG → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/svg-to-html.html): the artwork stays vector — sanitised with the svg + svgFilters profiles, so gradients and filters survive while scripts and event handlers are removed; the PNG/Word/PDF routes rasterise instead
- [CSV → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-html.html): SheetJS parses quotes and newlines inside fields, every row is written including the first, and values print as the file’s own characters because the CSV is read raw
- [CSV → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-markdown.html): the CSV becomes an HTML table and then a GitHub-flavoured pipe table, with a pipe inside a cell escaped and rows padded to the widest one
- [Markdown → CSV](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-csv.html): a pipe table becomes records with the first row as column names, written from values rather than display text, and one table at a time because several merge into an object the CSV step rejects
- [HTML → CSV](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-csv.html): rows and cells are read with a this-table-only scope so `th` headers cannot shift columns, and no remote reference on the page is ever fetched — one table per file, because two tables merge into an object the CSV stage rejects
- [Excel → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/excel-to-markdown.html): one pipe table per worksheet under its own heading, dates as ISO text and formulas as their results; several worksheets are fine here because the endpoint never meets the arrays-only gate
- [TXT → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-word.html): newlines, indentation and tabs survive into a .docx that carries the text as an MHTML altChunk, so Word decides the layout when it opens — faithful lines, no fixed typography
- [JSON → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-pdf.html): the syntax-coloured viewer is rendered expanded and sliced to A4, so the PDF shows the whole tree but has no text layer, and an over-tall document fails instead of truncating
- [JSON → TXT](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-txt.html): the structure survives as line breaks and `Array(n)` / `Object(n)` counts with strings still quoted, while the viewer’s indentation and colours are CSS and never become characters
- [CSV → TXT](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-txt.html): tab-separated rows that survive a comma inside a value, with the measured quirk that every line but the last keeps a trailing tab — aligned text to paste, not strict TSV
- [JSON → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-word.html): the structure viewer’s HTML is carried inside the .docx as an MHTML altChunk, so Word lays it out when it opens; measure, colour and folding are best-effort, and the counts arrive as text
- [Markdown → TXT](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-txt.html): markup becomes reading order — headings become lines, ordered lists are renumbered and nested with two spaces, links append their URL as `[text] [url]`, and images become `[Image: alt]`
- [TXT → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-html.html): the file’s characters are escaped and wrapped in `<pre>`, so nothing is interpreted as markup — a log or a code dump stays exactly as written, with the file name as the page title
- [JSON → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-html.html): a collapsible, syntax-coloured tree with `Array(n)` / `Object(n)` counts, every value escaped as text, and a non-recursive renderer so deep documents cannot blow the stack
- [HTML → JSON](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-json.html): one table becomes an array of objects with the first row as keys, `th` and `td` both counting as cells; several tables come back as one object grouped by their headings
- [Markdown → JSON](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-json.html): a pipe table becomes objects with the header row as keys and cell values left as strings, while several tables group under the document’s `<h2>` text — and a JSON code block is still honoured when there is no table
- [Markdown → Excel](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-excel.html): the table lands in a worksheet and a value becomes a number only if it round-trips byte-for-byte, so `00123` and `2024-01-05` keep their written form
- [TXT → JSON](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-json.html): when the `.txt` is really JSON, it comes back indented two spaces with numbers, booleans and `null` still themselves — and prose fails instead of being wrapped into a string
- [TXT → CSV](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-csv.html): a JSON array in the text becomes a table whose header is the union of every record’s keys, with bare elements caught by a synthetic `_value` column rather than dropped
- [JSON → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-md.html): the collapsible viewer’s lines land as text — keys, values and `Object(4)` summaries per paragraph, with no headings, no lists and no pipe table, because the intermediate HTML has none of those elements
- [JPG → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/jpg-to-html.html): the file’s raw bytes are embedded as a data URI with your basename as `alt` and `title` — no decode, no re-encode, self-contained, and about 4/3 the size
- [JPG → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/jpg-to-md.html): one self-contained image tag whose payload is the original file, with no OCR and no invented description — the extension never reads pixels and uploads nothing
- [PNG → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/png-to-docx.html): the packer lifts the data URI out of the markup into its own media part, so the .docx shows the picture offline with byte-identical pixels and alpha
- [JPG → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/jpg-to-docx.html): the same two-step embed as a media part inside the package, with no OCR — the words printed in the photo never become text
- [GIF → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif-to-html.html): the whole animation embedded verbatim as a data URI — no decode and no re-encode, so not one frame is dropped, though playback belongs to whatever opens the page
- [GIF → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif-to-md.html): one self-contained image tag whose base64 payload is the entire animation, with no first-frame grab; whether it plays, and whether a `data:` picture shows at all, is up to the reader
- [BMP → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/bmp-to-html.html): the raw bytes embedded as a data URI — no canvas and no re-encode, the opposite of BMP to PDF, which must decode onto a white-filled canvas; size goes up, never down
- [BMP → PDF](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/bmp-to-pdf.html): decoded onto a white ground and written as a lossless PNG stream, with the page sized from the pixels at 96 dpi rather than A4 — usually the one BMP exit that gets smaller
- [SVG → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/svg-to-docx.html): the vector becomes a bitmap in the second step, not the first — rasterised to PNG before sanitising, hoisted into an image part, and said out loud on the result card
- [WebP → HTML](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/webp-to-html.html): the whole file embedded as a data URI — alpha untouched and no frame reduction, though playback is the viewer’s call and the frame-loss check covers GIF only today
- [WebP → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/webp-to-md.html): one inline image tag holding the entire animation as base64; whether it plays, and whether a data URI picture renders at all, belongs to the reader
- [BMP → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/bmp-to-md.html): the whole uncompressed file inlined as base64 on one line — bytes untouched, but a BMP data URI does not render everywhere, so an external file is the safer shape
- [PNG → Markdown](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/png-to-md.html): one inline image tag holding the whole PNG as base64 — the alpha channel rides along untouched because this chain never opens a canvas, and display is the reader’s call
- [Word → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/docx-to-webp.html): a three-step chain that really produces a PDF in the middle — A4 render into lossless PNG slices, then one lossy WebP encode per page at the end
- [Excel → JPG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/xlsx-to-jpg.html): sheets to HTML, A4 paging through the browser, PNG slices inside a PDF, then JPEG at the endpoint — computed values only, never re-evaluated or executed
- [GIF → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif-to-docx.html): no frame-selection step on this chain — the whole animation is lifted into its own image part inside the .docx, while whether it plays is Word’s decision
- [TXT → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-png.html): the only text-to-image shape with no PDF inside — one continuous render at an 800 measure, failing clearly past 32768 px instead of arriving cropped
- [Word → JSON](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/docx-to-json.html): the output shape is set by how many tables the document has — one gives an array of objects, several become a grouped object (which the arrays-only CSV step refuses), and with none it parses the first code block
- [GIF → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/gif-to-webp.html): the first frame re-encoded as WebP — the animation goes, said with a fixed notice, but unlike JPEG no white ground is painted so the transparency keeps its alpha
- [TXT → Excel](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-xlsx.html): the text has to be a valid JSON array, and the workbook then keeps characters over guesses — round-trip values only become numbers, 16-digit ids stay pinned text
- [Word → JPG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/docx-to-jpg.html): embedded pictures arrive as data URIs and travel into the image, the layout is sliced into lossless A4 pages, and one JPEG per page lands in a ZIP from two pages up
- [Word → CSV](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/docx-to-csv.html): mammoth turns the document into HTML and the first table row supplies the keys, so `00424` and `2024-01-05` stay exactly as typed — and two tables in one file refuse the batch rather than guessing which one you meant
- [Word → Excel](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/docx-to-xlsx.html): the same three steps plus the typing rule of three, so a number returns only when its bytes do and 16-digit identifiers stay pinned text in one worksheet
- [HTML → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-webp.html): the same A4 slicing as the JPEG route with WebP as the final container — one image per page, a ZIP past two, quality and target size as the dials, and no claim about which container compresses smaller
- [Markdown → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-webp.html): GFM becomes layout first (real tables, inline SVG kept), then the same lossless A4 slices encoded WebP one page at a time; images referenced by URL have no bytes and are disclosed by count
- [HTML → JPG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-jpg.html): the document is rendered once and sliced into A4 pages stored as PNG, so one image per page with a single lossy pass at the end — transparent grounds go white, several pages arrive in a ZIP
- [Markdown → JPG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-jpg.html): GFM becomes layout first (real tables, inline SVG kept), then the same lossless A4 slicing with one JPEG per page; images referenced by URL have no bytes and are disclosed by count
- [CSV → JPG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-jpg.html): the table is written as lossless A4 PDF pages and only then JPEG-encoded, so one compression pass, one picture per page, several pages in a ZIP — and quality plus target size are real dials here
- [Excel → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/xlsx-to-png.html): every worksheet renders as a titled table and the whole stack is captured losslessly into one tall image, with the pixel density stepping down as the page grows and a 32768 px ceiling that fails rather than trimming
- [CSV → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-docx.html): read with `raw: true` into an HTML table and packed as an altChunk document, so `00424` and `2024-01-05` keep their characters while Word owns the layout — and the first row carries no header markup
- [CSV → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-png.html): one 800 px-wide lossless capture of the table, with 1px rules and striping from the bundled stylesheet, wrapping instead of widening, and a 32768 px height ceiling that fails rather than trimming
- [Markdown → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/markdown-to-png.html): GFM renders to the bundled stylesheet — striped tables, tinted code panels, inline SVG diagrams kept — and the whole page is captured losslessly, failing above 32768 px instead of trimming
- [JSON → PNG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-png.html): the collapsible viewer is captured as one lossless tall image — wrapping comes from layout, colour and indentation from pixels, and a page taller than 32768 px fails instead of trimming
- [JSON → JPG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/json-to-jpg.html): JPEG deliberately takes the PDF route, so a long file becomes A4 pages encoded one lossy time each, several pictures arriving in a ZIP
- [HTML → Excel](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/html-to-xlsx.html): a page table reaches one worksheet through JSON and CSV, where a value is a number only if its bytes come back exactly, so `00424` and 16-digit identifiers keep their written form
- [Excel → TXT](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/xlsx-to-txt.html): cells in worksheet order with tabs between them and an empty field kept as two adjacent tabs, so columns never shift; formulas arrive as their computed values
- [Why offline conversion, and where it stops](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/blog/): the long-form piece — what a browser can convert without a server, and which jobs genuinely need a desktop tool

## What it converts

- Documents: Markdown, HTML, Word (.docx), PDF, TXT — in any direction, through HTML as the hub format
- Data: CSV, Excel (.xlsx), JSON — in any direction, including CSV ⇄ XLSX and JSON ⇄ CSV
- Images: PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, GIF, SVG — readable; writable as PNG, JPEG or WebP (GIF uses its first frame, SVG is flattened). An inline SVG that travels into Word or Markdown is rasterized into an embedded PNG, because Word's HTML import does not draw inline SVG.
- Multi-step routes are discovered automatically: Markdown → HTML → PDF, Word → HTML → Markdown, JSON → CSV → XLSX, TXT → HTML → JSON → CSV → Excel
- 48 registered direct routes; breadth-first search over the same graph makes 143 source-to-target combinations reachable, and the format picker offers 116 of them. The other 27 are shown greyed-out with a reason rather than hidden (116 = 143 minus the 24 image→text/data and 3 PDF→data pairs listed below). Every source format reaches all 11 writable formats except itself.

## What it does not do (frequently asked of converters)

- No OCR: images cannot become TXT, CSV, JSON or XLSX (an OCR model would break the offline guarantee)
- PDF output is image-based and carries no text layer; text you manage to select in a PDF viewer was recognised by that viewer, not by this extension
- PDF input extracts text only; layout and embedded images are not preserved
- BMP, GIF and SVG are input-only — browsers expose no encoders for them
- No video, audio, e-book or CAD formats
- Limits: 100 MB per file (warned at 20 MB), 200 files per batch

## How it compares

| Dimension                         | Transfer Any File                                                             | Online converter                            | Command-line tool                                                  |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| File leaves the device            | Never                                                                         | Always (that is the mechanism)              | Never                                                              |
| Setup cost                        | Build once, load the unpacked folder                                          | None, it is a web page                      | Package manager and PATH                                           |
| Free-tier limits                  | 100 MB per file, 200 files per batch                                          | Daily quotas, size caps, watermarks         | None                                                               |
| Works offline                     | Yes                                                                           | No                                          | Yes                                                                |
| Batch of mixed formats            | Yes, one target for the whole batch                                           | Usually paid or queue-bound                 | Yes, and scriptable                                                |
| Preview and edit the result       | Built-in comparison view and inline editing                                   | Usually a thumbnail at best                 | None                                                               |
| Format breadth                    | 14 document / data / image formats                                            | Hundreds, including video and audio         | Pandoc 40+ document formats, ImageMagick hundreds of image formats |
| OCR and complex PDF layout repair | Not bundled                                                                   | Commonly offered                            | Requires a separate Tesseract install                              |
| Price and account                 | Free, no sign-up, no paid tier                                                | Free quota, a subscription lifts the limits | Usually free                                                       |
| Chinese interface and encoding    | Bilingual UI; CSV written with a UTF-8 BOM                                    | Depends on the service                      | Encoding is left to you                                            |
| Source code                       | Open source (MIT)                                                             | Closed                                      | Open source                                                        |

The comparison summarises the typical behaviour of each class of tool rather than one specific vendor; Pandoc and ImageMagick stand in for the command-line column. The three are not substitutes.

## How to install

One click from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/blkdmpkcaceicinkhindniepbbbaekkb) — the listing is live, and it is the build most users want. To install from source instead (Node.js ≥ 20.12, pnpm), build and load unpacked:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/liaolongdong/transfer-any-file
cd transfer-any-file
pnpm install && pnpm build
# chrome://extensions → enable Developer mode → Load unpacked → select .output/chrome-mv3
```

## Who maintains it

Sole author: Better ([github.com/liaolongdong](https://github.com/liaolongdong)). Contact channels, in the order they get answered: GitHub issues, email `924902324@qq.com` (also the address published on the store listing), and a WeChat group reached by adding `lld_1025` with the note `taf`. Security issues are reported privately, never as a public issue — see the security policy below. The same author maintains [Account Password Helper](https://github.com/liaolongdong/account-password-helper), a local-first password manager with the same no-cloud constraint.

- [Security policy](https://github.com/liaolongdong/transfer-any-file/blob/main/SECURITY.en.md): how to report a vulnerability, and the offline attack-surface claims you can verify ([简体中文](https://github.com/liaolongdong/transfer-any-file/blob/main/SECURITY.md))
- [Contributing guide](https://github.com/liaolongdong/transfer-any-file/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.en.md): the offline-only rule, how to add a converter, and which docs must move together ([简体中文](https://github.com/liaolongdong/transfer-any-file/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md))
- [Chrome Web Store listing copy and disclosures](https://github.com/liaolongdong/transfer-any-file/blob/main/.github/CHROMEWEBSTORE.md)

- [TXT → JPG](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-jpg.html): three steps with a PDF in the middle, so the result is one A4 sheet per image with a single lossy encode at the end — and long lines are clipped at the 734 px content box, never wrapped
- [TXT → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/txt-to-webp.html): the same A4 slicing through an intermediate PDF, ending in WebP instead of JPEG — usually smaller at comparable appearance, with the same clipped-not-wrapped warning about long lines

- [BMP → Word](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/bmp-to-docx.html): the raw bytes ride through HTML and are lifted into their own image part inside the .docx — no re-encode and no shrink, and a ZIP-unpacked file with no MIME type loses the picture entirely

- [CSV → WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/csv-to-webp.html): the table is set into an 800 px measure and paginated on A4 into lossless PNG slices inside a PDF, then encoded once at the WebP endpoint — wide columns are clipped, not wrapped
- [Excel to WebP](https://liaolongdong.github.io/transfer-any-file/convert/xlsx-to-webp.html): every sheet reaches the image under its own title, values are read and never re-evaluated, and cell styles or conditional formatting do not enter the intermediate HTML at all

## Tech stack

WXT · Vue 3 · TypeScript · Element Plus · Vite · Playwright (end-to-end). Heavy conversion libraries (marked, turndown, mammoth, pdf.js, SheetJS, jsPDF, html-to-image, DOMPurify) are dynamically imported per converter, and so is the ZIP packer (fflate) — loaded at the call site that needs it, not with the workbench. The complete bundle is 3.86 MB.
